title: Lifting shifted tower Hom bijections through a specified Roos triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be locally small pretriangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with countable products, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive exact functor with a specified natural comparison $F(K[m])\cong(FK)[m]$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$. Let $P,Q\in\mathcal C$, let $(T_n,t_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system], and put $B=\prod_{n\geq1}T_n$. Define $s:B\to B$ by $\pi_n s=t_n\pi_{n+1}$. Suppose a specified distinguished triangle is given:
$$Q\xrightarrow{q}B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\xrightarrow{d}Q[1].$$
This is a chosen Roos reconstruction, with its augmentation and connecting arrow, in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. Assume the canonical product comparison $\rho:FB\to\prod_nFT_n$, characterized by $\pi_n\rho=F(\pi_n)$, is an isomorphism. The image of the displayed triangle under $F$, transported through $\rho$ and the shift comparison, is the triangle used on $\mathcal D$; in particular its connecting arrow is the transported $F(d)$.

If for every $n\geq1$ and every $m\in\mathbf Z$ the map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P[m],T_n)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FP[m],FT_n),\qquad u\longmapsto F(u),$$
with source identified by the shift comparison, is bijective, then
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,Q)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FP,FQ),\qquad u\longmapsto F(u)$$
is bijective. This conclusion concerns the specified map of Hom groups, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between them; no vanishing of $R^1\varprojlim$ or Mittag--Leffler hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Remove the inverse source shift comparison from hT by cancellation of its isomorphism. Thus F.map on Hom(P[m],T_n) is bijective. For the product B, injectivity follows from the projections and these componentwise injections. For surjectivity lift every component b F(pi_n) to a_n, form a=Pi.lift(a_n), and compare F(a) rho with b rho by product extensionality. Cancel the isomorphism rho. This proves bijectivity on Hom(P[m],B); transport along the zero-shift isomorphism to obtain it on Hom(P,B).

Use the specified triangle S=(Q,B,B,q,v,d), v=1-s. Exactness of F gives its actual image triangle (FQ,FB,FB,Fq,Fv,Fd followed by the specified shift comparison). Work in this image triangle without transporting its product objects: cancellation of rho has already provided the required Hom bijections. Naturality gives F(u[1]) c_Q = c_P F(u)[1]. No independent target connecting arrow is chosen.

Prove the zero kernel of F.map on Hom(P,Q). If F(u)=0, injectivity on Hom(P,B) gives uq=0. Hom exactness gives u[1]=ad for a:P[1] to B. Shift naturality implies F(a) followed by the actual image connecting arrow is zero. Hom exactness in the image triangle factors F(a)=b_prime F(v). Lift b_prime to b:P[1] to B by product Hom surjectivity. Product Hom injectivity gives a=bv; since vd=0, u[1]=0. Faithfulness of shift implies u=0. Apply this to the difference of two maps to obtain injectivity.

For z:FP to FQ, lift z F(q) to b:P to B. Product Hom injectivity and qv=0 imply bv=0, so Hom exactness gives b=uq. Then (z-F(u)) F(q)=0. Exactness in the image triangle gives (z-F(u))[1]=a_prime F(d)c_Q. Lift c_P a_prime to a:P[1] to B by product Hom surjectivity. Fullness of shift supplies w:P to Q with w[1]=ad. Shift naturality yields c_P F(w)[1]=c_P(z-F(u))[1]. Cancel c_P and use faithfulness of shift to conclude F(w)=z-F(u). Therefore F(u+w)=z, proving surjectivity. This is the explicit kernel-and-image chase underlying the five lemma; the abstract abelian five-lemma declaration is unnecessary.
